title: Asir
capsule: The Emirate of Asir was a highland state in southwestern Arabia, corresponding roughly to the Asir region between the Hejaz and Yemen, that emerged under the Al-Idrisi family who rebelled against Ottoman authority in 1906–1908 and consolidated an independent emirate by around 1917. Muhammad ibn Ali al-Idrisi concluded a treaty with Britain in 1915 (the Treaty of Qunfudhah) aligning against the Ottomans, and the emirate controlled the port of Jizan and the fertile mountain highlands. After al-Idrisi's death in 1920 the dynasty fragmented, and Ibn Saud's Ikhwan forces invaded Asir in 1924, imposing Saudi suzerainty; the emirate was fully annexed by Saudi Arabia in 1934 following the defeat of Imam Yahya of Yemen who had contested the region.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent of the Emirate of Asir is poorly documented; its control over the highland interior was contested by both the Ottomans and later Saudi and Yemeni forces, and no precise boundaries were ever formally drawn.
